title: Quantized serving eviction and stability action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident ticket to track fixes and mitigations for a cluster of production regressions caused by quantized model serving. Multiple customer endpoints experienced pod evictions and crash loops when the int8 execution path encountered a dequantization operator ordering mismatch under long-context workloads. The incident caused elevated error rates and degraded generation quality for RLHF-style models during peak traffic windows.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 between 03:10-04:45 UTC several dedicated pools serving int8-quantized variants experienced progressive pod restarts and autoscaler evictions. A subset of rollouts that used on-the-fly fallback to float kernels also returned outputs with substantial accuracy drift compared to baseline. Root triggers: (1) a dequantization operator memory-accounting bug that leads to unbounded KV cache growth on certain sequence-length distributions, and (2) unsafe fallback paths that substitute a non-equivalent float kernel for an optimized int8 operator, producing subtle numerical drift for RLHF prompts.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Canary alert: pod restart rate increased in us-west-2 dedicated pool
2026-03-09 03:18 UTC - Pager triggered, SRE and inference-engineering paged in
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC - Rolled back recent quant-autotuner change in us-west-2 as immediate mitigation
2026-03-09 03:40 UTC - Identified KV-cache resident set growth correlated to dequant operator calls
2026-03-09 04:05 UTC - Enabled temporary per-pod memory limits and scaled up float-only fallback pool to shift traffic
2026-03-09 04:30 UTC - Deployed hotpatch disabling the new dequant fusion path (hotfix v1.20.3) to stop restarts
2026-03-09 04:45 UTC - Traffic normalized; customers notified and incident declared resolved for immediate availability
root_cause: Two interacting issues: (A) a codepath in the fused dequantization kernel that does not correctly account for per-request KV cache allocations when sequence length distributions are non-uniform, allowing memory usage to grow beyond expected reservations and triggering OOM/eviction; (B) the fallback mechanism that maps an unsupported int8 operator to a float kernel used an older numerical ordering that is not bit-equivalent, causing distributional shifts for RLHF-style scoring prompts and leading to perceived accuracy regressions.
mitigation_summary: Applied immediate rollback of the fused dequant path and deployed per-pod memory caps for dedicated pools. Rerouted traffic to float-only pools for affected customers while a safe kernel guard was implemented. Increased canary sampling for long-context prompts and added temporary alerting on per-op memory delta to detect re-emergence.
action_items: ENG-36422: Implement per-op memory accounting in runtime allocator and add unit tests to validate KV-cache lifecycle (owner: Liam Chen) - ETA 2026-03-18
ENG-36423: Add deterministic numerical equivalence tests for fallback kernels across representative RLHF prompt sets and include in canary pipeline (owner: Priya Kapoor) - ETA 2026-03-20
ENG-36424: Harden fallback gate: refuse runtime fallback if numerical equivalence check fails; provide explicit telemetry for operator fallbacks (owner: Marco Ruiz) - ETA 2026-03-17
ENG-36425: Expand canary suites to include long-context workloads with mixed short/long sequence distributions; run nightly accuracy regressions (owner: QA Team) - ETA 2026-03-14
ENG-36426: Add per-deployment memory histograms and per-op invocation counters to Console (owner: Observability) - ETA 2026-03-21
ENG-36427: Post-incident customer outreach: create tailored reports for affected customers with root cause and remediation timeline (owner: Customer Success) - ETA 2026-03-16
ENG-36428: Backfill model onboarding docs with explicit quantization compatibility checklist and supported-op matrix (owner: Model Onboarding) - ETA 2026-03-31
ENG-36429: Run canary rollout of guarded dequant fusion with staged traffic caps and automatic rollback on memory anomaly signals (owner: SRE/Release) - ETA 2026-03-22
followups: Schedule blameless postmortem review with engineering, SRE, product, and support (meeting: 2026-03-15)

status_update: Work on the per-op accounting hotfix is in progress; unit tests for KV-cache lifecycle are green in CI. Canary expansion scripts are merged to staging and nightly accuracy runs start 2026-03-14. Customer success has prepared initial outreach emails for impacted customers.
